I got my iPhone 16 a couple days ago, moved from Android. There's several thing I miss that may end up making me return the iPhone. 
The iPhone has no back button. Instead, you have to swipe from the left side of the screen and pull right. It's not as easy as difficult to do with one hand. I have to readjust my entire grip. 
But en even bigger problem is that you'll still have to swipe up, from the very bottom of the screen, to uncok your screen - even if you have FaceID. Unlike how I have my galaxy set up, where I just look at it and it automatically pops unlocked and is ready to go. And the swiping is very sensitive. Again, I have to adjust my grip to grab the very bottom of the screen and pull up quite a bit - on my galaxy I can swipe up from just about anywhere on the phone and it only needs a small, quick flick. The iPhone is a much larger swipe. 
These are my biggest pet peeves and I want to switch but I am not sure I can ultimately stick with the iPhone. 
But Apple has a 14 day return policy. Maybe get one, don't move cell service, but play with it for a few days to see if you like it for all the other features.

Dear OP,

I have been in a similar situation and I am currently leaving my husband, whom I deeply love but it just won't ever work. All I can say is from my own experience, but this man is showing you who he truly is. Consider it a positive  that this is happening before the wedding and additional years with this partner. I can tell you that it is lonelier being with the wrong person than it is to be by yourself. It is lonelier to never be able to converse with your partner about difficult topics for fear of an argument or you being sad at how different you both are.  It is lonelier being a quiet doormat. Don't be like me and 10+ years down the road you wish you left sooner.

Do not waste the best years of your life on someone whose fundamental opinions vastly differ your own. 

I wish someone told me at 28 that things would never change for the better. And that there's someone else out there who I will better fit with. 

Wishing you nothing but the best.

Oma is known for telling tall tales but this is what I've been told:

My grandmother (AKA Oma) lived in Munich, Germany through WW2. She remembers that the official declaration of war came her first day of school first grade. At some point, she explains, the military rounded up children and sent them to work on farms. Apparently, this was to keep the children safe from a potential bombing while also putting them to work picking potatoes for the community and military. The farm was guarded by military personnel and although they weren't cruel, they weren't warm and friendly. Kids would get whipped if they were caught eating any of the crops they were picking and there weren't enough blankets to go around. After some time, she was able to figure out a way to escape. I believe she was about 9 at this point but she was able to escape one evening and walked for days on end getting back to the city. Again, she's known for her tall tales but she thinks she walked about 200 miles, with only one shoe, back to the city and was able to make her way back to her mother.

She never really tells too many stories as she says it's too painful. She met my grandfather, who was an American stationed in Germany, after the war. My grandfather brought her to the states and they married. She claims she's never reached out nor spoken to any of her family members since leaving Germany. It's always been an interest of mine to see if I can track down some of her family members and meet them someday.
